title: Harness Design
description: Builds criterion-style harnesses with warmup, batching, and outlier rejection. Warmup settles caches and JITs; batching amortizes timer overhead; outlier rejection drops the noise. A good harness measures the code, not the measurement.
key_mechanisms: Warm up caches and JITs before timing

demo.title: Demo — Harness Design

title: Statistical Rigor
description: Reports confidence intervals and effect sizes instead of single best times. A result without uncertainty is a guess; the rigorous suite quantifies noise and only claims what the data supports. It ends arguments about whose laptop is faster.
key_mechanisms: Collect enough runs for stable stats

demo.title: Demo — Statistical Rigor

title: Regression Detection
description: Flags performance regressions over 3 percent against rolling baselines in CI. Baselines track recent history per hardware class, so the detector compares against reality, not a stale number. Regressions block the merge until explained.

demo.title: Demo — Regression Detection

title: Performance Baselines
description: Pins baselines per hardware class and OS version so comparisons are apples to apples. A benchmark number without its hardware context is meaningless. Baselines are re-pinned when the fleet changes.
key_mechanisms: Record hardware and OS with every run

demo.title: Demo — Performance Baselines

title: Micro vs Macro Balance
description: Pairs nanosecond microbenchmarks with end-to-end workload tests. Microbenchmarks find hot spots; macrobenchmarks prove user-visible wins. Suites that only do one or the other optimize the wrong thing.
key_mechanisms: Cover user journeys with macro tests
Require both to claim a win

demo.title: Demo — Micro vs Macro Balance

title: Workload Replay
description: Replays production traces as benchmark input for realism. Synthetic workloads lie; real traces capture the weird distributions production actually has. Traces are sampled and anonymized before replay.

demo.title: Demo — Workload Replay

title: CI Perf Gates
description: Blocks merges on statistically significant slowdowns. The gate runs the benchmark suite on every pull request and compares against the base branch. Performance becomes a reviewable property like correctness.

demo.title: Demo — CI Perf Gates

title: Hardware Normalization
description: Normalizes scores by CPU frequency and core count so results compare across machines. Raw times from different hardware are incomparable; normalization puts them on one scale. It enables fleet-wide performance tracking.
key_mechanisms: Record frequency and topology per run

demo.title: Demo — Hardware Normalization

title: Noisy-Neighbor Isolation
description: Pins benchmarks to isolated cores with IRQ affinity to escape noisy neighbors. Shared CI machines are chaos for timing; isolation makes results reproducible. The harness verifies isolation before trusting numbers.

demo.title: Demo — Noisy-Neighbor Isolation

title: Benchmark Sharding
description: Splits long suites across parallel runners to keep CI under ten minutes. Shards are balanced by historical runtime so no shard dominates. Results merge into one report.

demo.title: Demo — Benchmark Sharding

title: Result Databases
description: Stores every benchmark run in a time-series database for trend analysis. History turns one-off numbers into trends, and trends reveal slow regressions that single runs miss. Dashboards make the trends visible.
key_mechanisms: Store every run with full context

demo.title: Demo — Result Databases

title: Flakiness Quarantine
description: Quarantines benchmarks with high variance until they stabilize. A flaky benchmark cries wolf and trains teams to ignore the suite. Quarantine keeps the suite trustworthy while the benchmark is fixed.

demo.title: Demo — Flakiness Quarantine

title: A/B Perf Experiments
description: Runs interleaved A/B trials to cancel environmental drift. Instead of benchmarking old then new, it alternates them so temperature and load affect both equally. The paired design needs fewer runs for the same confidence.

demo.title: Demo — A/B Perf Experiments

title: Energy Benchmarks
description: Measures joules per operation alongside time. On mobile and in dense datacenters, energy is a first-class cost. The harness reads RAPL counters around each benchmark for per-operation energy.

demo.title: Demo — Energy Benchmarks

title: Benchmark Minimization
description: Selects the minimal benchmark subset that still catches historical regressions. Running everything on every commit is too slow; the minimizer keeps the benchmarks that actually caught past problems. Coverage of past regressions is the selection criterion.
key_mechanisms: Record which benchmarks caught past regressions

demo.title: Demo — Benchmark Minimization
